_doc: Single source of truth for the Nexus memory routing rules. This machine-readable artifact encodes the same rule sets that skills/nexus-memory/SKILL.md describes in prose. BOTH consume this ONE artifact: hooks/memory_capture.py loads it at runtime to decide whether/how to nudge, and SKILL.md references it by path. Do NOT duplicate or diverge these rules in either consumer (single-rule-set invariant, proposal D2/D5/D3; parity enforced by the T4 test). TWO rule families share this one file: (1) the WRITE/lifetime-axis capture partition (capture_positive / transient_negative) → nudges nexus.memory_create; (2) the READ-intent partition (read_allowlist / read_timetravel_markers / read_blocklist) → nudges nexus.context_retrieve on cross-session recall (mcp-read-path-routing FU, proposal D1/D5). The single hook checks WRITE intent first, then READ — mutually-exclusive dispatch (D3). All patterns are lowercase Python `re` regex evaluated against the lowercased prompt. WRITE classification is by LIFETIME (durable cross-session vs transient within-session), never by topic. Capture iff a capture_positive pattern matches AND no transient_negative pattern matches (negative overrides — D7 / over-capture bound). READ classification is LEXICAL not semantic (proposal D1, precision-first): fire ONLY on the explicit first-person recall allowlist AND no read_blocklist override (imperative coding / third-person general knowledge / project-static / within-session referents must NOT fire). If a read_timetravel_marker also matches → time-travel route (context_retrieve + relative as_of within 90 days, D5). CALIBRATION NOTES (deferred to measured dogfood, not blind-tightened): (a) broad WRITE reaction verbs 'i like'/'i love'/'i work' can over-fire on transient usage ('I like that approach for this file') — kept because they also carry genuine durable preferences; tighten only if measured. (b) trailing '?' is a HARD ignore for the WRITE path (questions are usually recalls) — it will silence the occasional question-framed durable write by design; questions are instead the READ path's domain. The nudge is advisory + self-bounded, so false positives cannot force a tool call.

_read_doc: READ-intent partition (mcp-read-path-routing FU, proposal D1/D5). Consumed by the SAME hook (hooks/memory_capture.py) as the WRITE rules above — one hook, two rule sections (D3). Dispatch order: WRITE intent (capture_positive AND not transient_negative) is checked FIRST; only if that does not fire does the hook evaluate READ. READ fires ONLY when a read_allowlist pattern matches AND NO read_blocklist pattern matches (blocklist OVERRIDES allowlist — precision-first, D1). On a read hit: if a read_timetravel_markers pattern ALSO matches → 'timetravel' route (nudge nexus.context_retrieve WITH a relative as_of inside the last 90 days, D5); else → 'recall' route (nudge nexus.context_retrieve, NO as_of). The authority assertion in the nudge is scoped to recall hits ONLY — never a blanket 'always prefer Nexus' (max over-fire, D1). Classification is LEXICAL, not semantic: only explicit first-person cross-session recall fires. All patterns are lowercase Python `re` regex against the lowercased prompt. READ CALIBRATION NOTES (deferred to measured T6 dogfood, not blind-tightened — code-review 2026-06-20): (a) WRITE-FIRST SHADOWING: a time-named recall that ALSO contains a possessive-preference write phrase ('last week i told you my preferred X', 'back in May i decided my favourite Y') currently routes WRITE, because past-time markers (last week/last month/back in <month>) are NOT in transient_negative so the write check fires first. Fix from measured data: add those past-time markers to transient_negative, OR evaluate read_timetravel_markers before committing to WRITE (time-named ⇒ recall-dominant). The dogfood S5 prompt ('set a preference … what was it') does not hit this; T6 should probe 'last week i … my preferred …'. (b) BROAD-VERB RECALL SUPPRESSION: read_blocklist's verb list (make/add/build/update/change…) silently suppresses legitimate recalls containing those common verbs ('what's my default make target') — a deliberate precision-first false-negative; widen only if measured recall is poor.
